findings.title: An offline rename of a pending workspace is silently dropped when its folder later carries another id
findings.body:
The change at registry.ts:634 keeps `pendingInit` after an edit made while the folder is away, and registry.ts:637-638 sets `pendingIdentity` for that edit. Before this change, the edit cleared `pendingInit`.

Now take the case where the folder comes back with an identity.json whose id is not registered on this Mac (for example, written by another Mac that uses the same drive). `availability` reaches the adoption branch at registry.ts:718-727. There, `Object.assign(entry, entryFromIdentity(...))` at line 724 replaces `name` and `color` with the folder's values. It does not clear `pendingIdentity`, so the entry keeps the flag while now holding the folder's name. The offline rename the user made is gone. The edit had told the user it would reach the folder (workspaces-context.tsx:158-160). On the next probe, registry.ts:670-672 writes the folder's own name back over the file, so nothing shows the loss.

Before this change the same sequence ended differently: `pendingInit` was already cleared, so the adoption branch was skipped, the probe returned `different`, and the renamed name stayed in the registry.

Suggested fix for this failure: do not take the adoption branch when `entry.pendingIdentity` is set, which restores the earlier outcome. The other option is to keep the pending name and tell the user it was replaced. The adoption rule for pending entries without an offline edit is not changed by this. registry.test.ts:210 covers adoption without any edit, so it does not exercise this case. This is a different path from the deferred `relocate` refusal in the open thread on registry.ts:809.

findings.title: The silent path for an unchanged folder has no renderer test
findings.body: `onRelocated` now returns early when `result.unchanged` is set (line 168). No test under `features/workspaces` checks this. `workspace-dialog.test.tsx` only mocks `onRelocated`, and the main-side test at relocate.test.ts:158 pins the flag but not the toast. If the early return were removed, every test would still pass and the "now points to the new folder" toast would come back for the Settings and dialog paths. Add a case to the context or dialog tests that resolves `relocate` with `{ ok: true, unchanged: true, workspace }` and asserts that no toast is shown.

contracts.action: Change folder… on the folder the workspace already points at (same path picked again)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/switch-transaction.ts:96-137 (relocateActive, the transaction used for every other change to the active workspace)
contracts.before_after: Before: for the active workspace, the same-path pick still ran relocateActive: prepareWindows, gate.close, apply (registry.relocate, which persists), dropPendingCaptures, afterCommit (gate.commit bumps the generation). After: the same-path check returns { ok: true, entry, unchanged: true } before any of those steps. index.ts still runs the probe and the broadcast after the result (index.ts:342-345).
contracts.visible_effect: No unsaved-editor question, no captures dropped, no route remount, and no 'now points to the new folder' toast (workspaces-context.tsx:166-168).

contracts.action: Rename or recolor a workspace while its folder is not connected, on an entry still marked pendingInit
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts:637-638 (the pendingIdentity branch of the same update, which the edit already used for the other pending flags)
contracts.before_after: Before: the edit always deleted pendingInit, so the entry became an ordinary pending-identity entry. After: pendingInit stays when the folder was not written (savedToFolder false), so the entry keeps accepting a moved folder that has Kaipu items and no identity (registry.ts:851-855), and it can reach the adoption branch at registry.ts:718-727.
contracts.visible_effect: The offline edit is accepted and the move-folder check accepts the workspace's new folder (registry-relocate.test.ts:221-243).
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder later comes back with an identity.json holding an unregistered id, the adoption branch replaces the offline name and color with the folder's values (registry.ts:724) and keeps pendingIdentity, so the rename is lost silently. See the finding on registry.ts:724.

contracts.action: Renderer receives an unchanged relocate result and skips the toast (dialog and Settings)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/workspaces/workspaces-context.tsx:169 (the same onRelocated callback's toast for a real change)
contracts.before_after: Before: every ok result showed the folderChanged toast. After: an ok result with unchanged: true returns before the toast. Both callers reach onRelocated the same way: workspace-dialog.tsx:144-145 and workspaces-context.tsx:184-186.
contracts.visible_effect: No toast when the picked folder is the same one. The dialog stays open with no message, as before the change.

contracts.action: IPC handler passes the unchanged flag through to the renderer
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts:346-349 (the same handler's ok return, which already carries workspace)
contracts.before_after: Before: the ok result had only workspace. After: it also carries unchanged: true when relocateWorkspace set it. Same refresh and broadcast steps before the return.
contracts.visible_effect: Only the renderer toast decision, as in the previous entry.
contracts.failure_mode: If the flag were dropped here, the renderer would show the 'now points' toast for the same folder again. No test covers this handler (index.ts imports electron).

thread_replies.reply: Checked the current code: the rollback in `edit` (registry.ts:643-647) restores the old identity.json when there was one and removes the new one when there was none, so the absent branch is in place.
Checked: `createWorkspace` (index.ts:272-274) reports `invalid-name` and `invalid-color` as separate checks.
Checked: `edit` re-runs `validateWorkspaceName` inside the locked `update` (registry.ts:624-626) and throws `NameTakenError`, which maps to `name-taken`.

Partly addressed: a pendingInit folder with no identity.json is now accepted (registry.ts:851-855). The other case, a moved folder that holds another id, is still refused by `checkRelocate` as the owner decided, and that follow-up is still open. Separately, this change opens a new path into the adoption branch in `availability` (registry.ts:718-727) that drops an offline rename. That is in a new finding on registry.ts:724.
Checked: `relocateWorkspace` returns the unchanged entry before `relocateActive` (relocate.ts:42-45), so no window is asked to save, no capture is dropped and the generation stays.

Checked: `relocateWorkspace` now returns `unchanged: true` (relocate.ts:43-45), `relocateFolder` passes it on (index.ts:349), and `onRelocated` returns before the toast (workspaces-context.tsx:168). The test at relocate.test.ts:158 asserts the flag.

structuredOutput.summary: Reviewed the seven files of part 1 in full, plus the relocate path they feed (switch-transaction.ts, identity.ts, workspace-dialog.tsx) and the registry tests. The `unchanged` flag, its IPC pass-through, the renderer skip and the same-folder early return are consistent. The `edit` change that keeps `pendingInit` after an offline edit is correct for the case its new test covers. It opens a path the adoption branch in `availability` did not reach before, and there the offline rename is dropped silently (finding on registry.ts:724, medium confidence). One test gap is reported for the renderer skip. Six open threads on this part's files were checked: five are addressed, and the registry.ts:809 thread is still open for the other-id case the owner deferred.

It does not clear `pendingIdentity`, so the entry keeps the flag while now holding the folder's name. The offline rename the user made is gone. The edit had told the user it would reach the folder (workspaces-context.tsx:158-160). On the next probe, registry.ts:670-672 writes the folder's own name back over the file, so nothing shows the loss.

Before this change the same sequence ended differently: `pendingInit` was already cleared, so the adoption branch was skipped, the probe returned `different`, and the renamed name stayed in the registry.

Suggested fix for this failure: do not take the adoption branch when `entry.pendingIdentity` is set, which restores the earlier outcome. The other option is to keep the pending name and tell the user it was replaced. The adoption rule for pending entries without an offline edit is not changed by this. registry.test.ts:210 covers adoption without any edit, so it does not exercise this case. This is a different path from the deferred `relocate` refusal in the open thread on registry.ts:809.

findings.title: The silent path for an unchanged folder has no renderer test
findings.body: `onRelocated` now returns early when `result.unchanged` is set (line 168). No test under `features/workspaces` checks this. `workspace-dialog.test.tsx` only mocks `onRelocated`, and the main-side test at relocate.test.ts:158 pins the flag but not the toast. If the early return were removed, every test would still pass and the "now points to the new folder" toast would come back for the Settings and dialog paths. Add a case to the context or dialog tests that resolves `relocate` with `{ ok: true, unchanged: true, workspace }` and asserts that no toast is shown.

contracts.action: Change folder… on the folder the workspace already points at (same path picked again)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/switch-transaction.ts:96-137 (relocateActive, the transaction used for every other change to the active workspace)
contracts.before_after: Before: for the active workspace, the same-path pick still ran relocateActive: prepareWindows, gate.close, apply (registry.relocate, which persists), dropPendingCaptures, afterCommit (gate.commit bumps the generation). After: the same-path check returns { ok: true, entry, unchanged: true } before any of those steps. index.ts still runs the probe and the broadcast after the result (index.ts:342-345).
contracts.visible_effect: No unsaved-editor question, no captures dropped, no route remount, and no 'now points to the new folder' toast (workspaces-context.tsx:166-168).

contracts.action: Rename or recolor a workspace while its folder is not connected, on an entry still marked pendingInit
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/registry.ts:637-638 (the pendingIdentity branch of the same update, which the edit already used for the other pending flags)
contracts.before_after: Before: the edit always deleted pendingInit, so the entry became an ordinary pending-identity entry. After: pendingInit stays when the folder was not written (savedToFolder false), so the entry keeps accepting a moved folder that has Kaipu items and no identity (registry.ts:851-855), and it can reach the adoption branch at registry.ts:718-727.
contracts.visible_effect: The offline edit is accepted and the move-folder check accepts the workspace's new folder (registry-relocate.test.ts:221-243).
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder later comes back with an identity.json holding an unregistered id, the adoption branch replaces the offline name and color with the folder's values (registry.ts:724) and keeps pendingIdentity, so the rename is lost silently. See the finding on registry.ts:724.

contracts.action: Renderer receives an unchanged relocate result and skips the toast (dialog and Settings)
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/workspaces/workspaces-context.tsx:169 (the same onRelocated callback's toast for a real change)
contracts.before_after: Before: every ok result showed the folderChanged toast. After: an ok result with unchanged: true returns before the toast. Both callers reach onRelocated the same way: workspace-dialog.tsx:144-145 and workspaces-context.tsx:184-186.
contracts.visible_effect: No toast when the picked folder is the same one. The dialog stays open with no message, as before the change.

contracts.action: IPC handler passes the unchanged flag through to the renderer
contracts.equivalent_path: apps/kaipu-record/src/main/workspaces/index.ts:346-349 (the same handler's ok return, which already carries workspace)
contracts.before_after: Before: the ok result had only workspace. After: it also carries unchanged: true when relocateWorkspace set it. Same refresh and broadcast steps before the return.

contracts.failure_mode: If the flag were dropped here, the renderer would show the 'now points' toast for the same folder again. No test covers this handler (index.ts imports electron).

thread_replies.reply: Checked the current code: the rollback in `edit` (registry.ts:643-647) restores the old identity.json when there was one and removes the new one when there was none, so the absent branch is in place.
Checked: `createWorkspace` (index.ts:272-274) reports `invalid-name` and `invalid-color` as separate checks.
Checked: `edit` re-runs `validateWorkspaceName` inside the locked `update` (registry.ts:624-626) and throws `NameTakenError`, which maps to `name-taken`.

Partly addressed: a pendingInit folder with no identity.json is now accepted (registry.ts:851-855). The other case, a moved folder that holds another id, is still refused by `checkRelocate` as the owner decided, and that follow-up is still open. Separately, this change opens a new path into the adoption branch in `availability` (registry.ts:718-727) that drops an offline rename. That is in a new finding on registry.ts:724.
Checked: `relocateWorkspace` returns the unchanged entry before `relocateActive` (relocate.ts:42-45), so no window is asked to save, no capture is dropped and the generation stays.

Checked: `relocateWorkspace` now returns `unchanged: true` (relocate.ts:43-45), `relocateFolder` passes it on (index.ts:349), and `onRelocated` returns before the toast (workspaces-context.tsx:168). The test at relocate.test.ts:158 asserts the flag.

structured_output.summary: Reviewed the seven files of part 1 in full, plus the relocate path they feed (switch-transaction.ts, identity.ts, workspace-dialog.tsx) and the registry tests. The `unchanged` flag, its IPC pass-through, the renderer skip and the same-folder early return are consistent. The `edit` change that keeps `pendingInit` after an offline edit is correct for the case its new test covers. It opens a path the adoption branch in `availability` did not reach before, and there the offline rename is dropped silently (finding on registry.ts:724, medium confidence). One test gap is reported for the renderer skip. Six open threads on this part's files were checked: five are addressed, and the registry.ts:809 thread is still open for the other-id case the owner deferred.
